expected_approaches.summary: Store prefix products in the output, then multiply each position by a rolling suffix product.
expected_approaches.applicability: Array products when division is disallowed.
assumptions: The output array is not counted as auxiliary storage by the stated optimization.
key_invariants: Before the reverse pass, output[i] is the product strictly left of i.
During the reverse pass, suffix is the product strictly right of i.
tradeoffs: Requires two directional passes and careful initialization.
common_failure_modes: including nums[i] in a prefix or suffix

alternative_approaches.summary: Build explicit left and right product arrays, then combine them.
alternative_approaches.applicability: A clearer first implementation when extra memory is acceptable.
tradeoffs: More transparent but consumes two auxiliary arrays.

alternative_approaches.summary: Use total product only after separately accounting for zero counts.
alternative_approaches.applicability: A variant only when division is permitted and numeric behavior is controlled.
assumptions: Division and overflow semantics are acceptable.
key_invariants: Zero count determines whether division is meaningful.
tradeoffs: Violates the primary no-division requirement and complicates zeros.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: vector<int> productExceptSelf(vector<int> nums){ int n=nums.size(); vector<int> out(n,1); int prefix=1; for(int i=0;i<n;i++){out[i]=prefix; prefix*=nums[i];} int suffix=1; for(int i=n-1;i>=0;i--){out[i]*=suffix; suffix*=nums[i];} return out; } };

class Solution { public int[] productExceptSelf(int[] nums){ int[] out=new int[nums.length]; int prefix=1; for(int i=0;i<nums.length;i++){out[i]=prefix; prefix*=nums[i];} int suffix=1; for(int i=nums.length-1;i>=0;i--){out[i]*=suffix; suffix*=nums[i];} return out; } }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: Each output entry combines products strictly before and after its own index.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Explain why two passes remain linear and why output reuse changes auxiliary space.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Recognize that total-product division fails with zeros.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Update the rolling product after using it for the current output position.
Multiply by the current suffix before incorporating nums[i].

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: Only the zero position can be nonzero.
Every result is zero when at least two zeros occur.

counterexamples.purpose: Exposes division and inclusion mistakes around one zero.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Discuss why division still needs zero accounting and numeric caution.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend that neither rolling product includes the current value.
Test a division proposal against zero inputs.

common_followups.diagnostic_goal: Test the order of each rolling update.
weak_or_misconception_signals: includes nums[i] in its own answer

weak_or_misconception_signals: divides by zero or ignores it
sample_phrasings: What happens to your division approach when the input contains zero?

expected_good_signals: separates returned output from extra arrays
